reference: ffprobe of FFmpeg 9.0.2, the decode profile of cargo xtask prepare-ffmpeg (.research/reference-decode/install/bin/ffprobe), -show_packets with the demuxer forced
candidate: codec-worker packets FORMAT FILE: every packet triergon_ogg::BlockingReader or the triergon_elementary reader of FORMAT emits, as the reader reports it, and for Ogg also the reader's FFmpeg-compatible view (triergon_ogg::compat::clock::packet_timing)

views.native: what the reader reports: its own times, durations and trims
views.compat: the reader's FFmpeg-compatible policy of the same packets; a native difference this view does not have is reproduced-by-compat and needs no disposition

rules.rule: both sides read the file with the format of its manifest lane: ffprobe -f ogg|flac|mp3|aac|ac3|eac3, codec-worker the same reader
rules.reason: the comparison is of one reader against one demuxer; probing could pick a different one on either side

rules.rule: per stream, packets are aligned in order at the least cost (a pair costs the number of its aligned field and size that differ, an unpaired packet 1; of equal costs a pair is preferred); every unpaired packet is an 'unmatched' difference and every compared field of every pair is compared; a stream only one side has packets in is one 'packets' difference of the two counts; the set of streams and whether reading ended in an error are compared too
rules.reason: a reader emits packets in file order; aligning keeps one extra or merged packet from shifting every later pair, while nothing is skipped: an unpaired packet is a difference like any other

rules.scope: pts, dts and duration of both views
rules.rule: the reader's ticks are rescaled into the FFmpeg stream time base when every time converts exactly; otherwise each duration is rounded down and the times accumulate from the first packet's time
rules.reason: FFmpeg times elementary streams in a fixed base (MPEG audio 1/14112000, ADTS 1/28224000, AC-3 1/90000) and, where a frame's sample count does not divide it (AC-3 at 44.1 kHz), its parser rounds each duration down and adds them up

rules.rule: an absent trim equals a trim of zero: the reader's Trim::start and Trim::end (compat: skip_samples and discard_padding) against the skip_samples and discard_padding of FFmpeg's skip-samples side data
rules.reason: FFmpeg attaches the side data only to packets it trims and writes both values when it does

rules.rule: the reader's n-th track of every chain link is FFmpeg's stream n
rules.reason: FFmpeg's Ogg demuxer replaces a link's streams in place when a chained link starts, where the reader opens new tracks

rules.rule: the reader's duration is compared with FFmpeg's duration plus the packet's discard padding
rules.reason: FFmpeg's Ogg demuxer shortens the last packet's duration by the discard padding it reports; the reader keeps the coded duration and reports the padding as Trim::end, which is compared separately. The compat view reports FFmpeg's shortened duration and is compared as it is

rules.rule: the compat view's dts is its pts
rules.reason: the policy reports one time for presentation and decode, as FFmpeg's Ogg demuxer does

rules.rule: packet positions are not compared; Ogg packets are aligned by size
rules.reason: the reader reports the page that completes a packet and FFmpeg the page it starts on, so the two differ by definition for every packet that spans pages

rules.rule: the reader's one track is FFmpeg's first audio stream; packets of other streams are counted in the row (reference_other_packets) and not compared
rules.reason: FFmpeg turns an ID3v2 picture into an attached-picture video stream; the reader keeps tag bytes as tags, not packets

rules.rule: a difference neither view explains must be one of the reviewed differences of its case and view in harness/codecs/reader-differences.json (by their SHA-256), and fall within the scope (view, field, packets and value relation) of exactly one disposition the case lists, the one it was reviewed under; a case listing a disposition that covers none of its differences fails
rules.reason: a disposition explains only the kind of difference it names, on the packets it names

dispositions.reason: FFmpeg times the last Ogg page forwards from its first packet; when the page's granule position precedes its last packet's start, that packet's duration is negative and ffprobe prints it modulo 2^32. The compat view keeps it negative; the native view's coded duration is compared with FFmpeg's plus the padding, which carries the same 2^32
when the first audio page fails its CRC, FFmpeg times the first packet it keeps from that packet's page; the compat view times it from the stream start, as if the lost packets had been delivered

when the sample rate changes, FFmpeg delivers each FLAC frame's duration rescaled to the first frame's rate; the reader times every frame at its own rate. The reader reports no per-frame rate, so the scope is every duration
FFmpeg delivers FLAC frames at 768 kHz without a duration and the last one without a time; the reader times them from the frame headers

FFmpeg's FLAC parser times the last frame of a stream at the previous packet's end (its time plus its duration as FFmpeg reports it), not from the frame's own number; this shows where block sizes vary under the fixed-blocking flag and where FFmpeg's durations differ from the frames' (a sample rate change, a time base taken from leading bytes); the reader times every frame from its frame number

FFmpeg merges a damaged FLAC frame with the frames after it into one packet without times, spanning the bytes of the reader's packets; the reader ends the damaged frame at the next header its CRC-16 confirms

after a packet FFmpeg's FLAC parser assembled from bytes the reader does not deliver as that packet (leading bytes, a merged damaged frame), it reports the next packet's position as its own read position; the reader reports the frame's source offset

in a FLAC stream without STREAMINFO that starts with unparsable bytes, FFmpeg takes the stream time base (1/32000) from a frame header in those bytes but times packets in samples of the stream rate; its times are the reader's sample times unconverted

FFmpeg delivers the bytes before the first FLAC or AC-3 frame as a packet and times the frames after it from that packet's end; the reader keeps leading tags as tags and skips junk to the first confirmed frame
FFmpeg delivers the 128-byte ID3v1 tag at the end of a FLAC or AC-3 stream as part of the last packet; the reader keeps it as a tag

FFmpeg accepts an MPEG audio frame of another version or sample rate, or a header in junk that no frame follows, cutting the same bytes into other packets and timing later frames after them; the reader requires the frame after a header to confirm it
FFmpeg 9.0.2 refuses free-format MPEG audio; the reader delivers its frames
FFmpeg reports ADTS packet positions after junk as if the junk were not there; the reader reports each frame's source offset, one constant offset (the junk) later
FFmpeg refuses to open a FLAC stream whose STREAMINFO declares a maximum block size below 16; that is a decoder decision, so the reader still delivers the frames

a metadata block whose length runs past the end of the file: FFmpeg declares the stream STREAMINFO describes and delivers no packets; the reader refuses the stream as truncated, since no frame can follow the metadata
